acceptance:
Build a Lean proof that produces the finite proper-loss forest of Lemma 3.1 on a flat quotient DAG. Work on the iteration across the topological order, not another proof of pair-key reuse or the predecessor cases. Represent each real key by one canonically ordered CutPair. Provide a parent, an artificial root, and one label per vertex. Prove inclusive ancestor correctness, exactly the effective keys, no repeated nodes, at most vertexCount real nodes, child endpoints lost by the parent, proper-loss nesting, and both parent endpoints precede every fresh endpoint. The input order may be a supplied topological enumeration with its completeness and distinct-order proofs. EX2.1 first-loss arc characterization already builds. Use one candidate two-predecessor key per vertex to bound the number of nodes.

Suggested route: define chains by well-founded recursion on topological rank or a fold over the enumerated vertices. For a nontrivial vertex, read the latest predecessor's validated chain, select the qualifying prefix, and append the optional exact canonical predecessor key. The conditional local transition's exact interface is supplied. A candidate key's immediate parent is the last node of this prefix; the parent agrees across all witnesses of the same pair because the predecessor set, latest predecessor and its earlier label agree. A first proper loss witnesses every effective key. Prove the selected chains follow the single stored parent relation. If the entire construction exceeds this turn, give the strongest complete theorem for the global induction and identify the first missing proof in a checkpoint. Deliver standalone Lean in module PaperB.Forest. Use the published Lemma 3.1 acceptance criteria.

Implement the v1.3 growing-tree skew-binary parent/depth/jump kernel in Lean. Define append-only leaves including multiple branches, an artificial root with depth zero and jump to itself, and depth-target traversal. Store one parent, one depth and one jump per node. Insertion merges the first two equal positive jumps with the new leading node; otherwise it stores the parent. Prove that updates preserve earlier records, traversal returns the unique ancestor at the requested depth, and that a trace contains O(L) moves for L=ceil(log2(n+2)). You may prove natural-number bounds with a single uniform constant under n+2 ≤ 2^L, then relate them to the final word model separately. Charge insertion constant record operations and linear records. Nested block sizes 2^k−1, strict increase except a possible leading tie, and descent into at most one half-block supply the cost proof. Include root/depth zero, nontrivial branching, and the merge case. Deliver standalone Lean in module PaperB.Jumps. Identify the exact outstanding word-model bridge if EX0.3 is needed for an actual RAM claim.

Prove the finite executable forest constructor of v1.3 Lemma 3.2 against exactly the forest and jump interfaces. Start with the deterministic predecessor preprocessing and prefix-probe cost, which can be developed independently. Deduplicate vertex IDs per head without collapsing the physical quotient arcs. Count at most n_H candidate keys, handle duplicate keys, maintain the previous record for reuse, and use an ordered key dictionary plus final ancestry intervals. A known node query uses constant operations; pair-key lookup is O(L). Show each binary search uses at most O(L) probes and charges each ancestor selection and each predecessor scan at O(L) per item. Prove O((n_H+m_H)L²) preprocessing, O(n_H+m_H) peak working words and O(n_H) retained words as operational claims for the same program. If earlier forest or jump implementations are still arriving, prove the interface-relative charging theorem in standalone Lean and explain which actual program and word-model bridges remain. Never call that conditional result a proof of the full bound. Deliver module PaperB.ForestBuild, with imports made explicit in the progress note.
